source.title: Analysis of the Scalability of a Deep-Learning Network for Steganography "Into the Wild"
source.authors: Hugo Ruiz; M. Chaumont; M. Yedroudj; A. Amara; F. Comby; G. Subsol

page_placements.theme: Monotone or saturating learning curves in specified settings

record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses double descent and studies training-data scaling, but its experiment is deliberately set in the assumed power-law region rather than testing a double-descent peak or its location.
record.gate_note: The paper reports test accuracy for LC-Net at four training-set sizes. It says it chose a dataset size that avoids the small-data region where error may rise, and assumes the power-law regime applies. The reported power-law extrapolations to 2M and 20M images are predictions, not experimental measurements.
record.test_reason: The paper only discusses double descent. Its single experiment sweeps training-set size for one fixed 300k-parameter steganalysis CNN, and the authors chose the setup to avoid double descent. The payload and the 20k minimum were picked to stay out of the small-data region where error can rise (footnote 5). Training used near-optimal early stopping, which the authors note is needed because LC-Net may sit near the interpolation threshold. So the data sweep is set in the assumed power-law region. It is not a test of whether more data hurts near the threshold, and there is no model-size, epoch, noise or regularization sweep.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that the data-scaling error power law holds for deep-learning steganalysis even with a medium-size network and a diverse database. They also conclude that performance does not collapse as the database grows, and that more than one million images are likely needed before reaching the irreducible-error region. They do not test or report a double-descent peak.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies training-data scaling for one fixed steganalysis network in an assumed power-law regime; it does not reproduce the original double-descent sweeps.

fits_no_version.finding: For LC-Net on LSSD JPEG steganalysis, test accuracy rises monotonically from 62.33% to 68.31% between 20k and 1M training images. The error fits a power law with a fitted floor of about 16.8%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Data-scaling power law: in the power-law region, test error falls as a power law of training-set size, here in steganalysis with a medium-size CNN.

record.peer_reviewed: ICPR’2021 Workshop on MultiMedia FORensics in the WILD, Lecture Notes in Computer Science, Springer
record.problems: Only four training-set sizes were evaluated; the 1,000,000-image result is from one test. The paper states that 1M and 2M cover-set experiments were not run because of training time. Its estimate of irreducible error is described as uncertain, and larger-set outcomes are extrapolations.
record.rows_left_out: No reported experimental outcomes on model size, epochs, noise, regularization, or interpolation-threshold behavior. Predicted error values for 2M and 20M images are extrapolations rather than measured results.

untested.parts: No model-size sweep; only one fixed 300k-parameter network.
The sample-size effect near the interpolation threshold is not tested. The setup deliberately avoids the small-data region and uses early stopping.
No capacity sweep across model classes.
No effective-complexity measure or prediction of peak location.
No variation of label noise or regularization, and no multiple-peak analysis.

record.verdict_notes: Agree with the reader's T6/discusses classification. The only link to double descent is the authors' remark that LC-Net is 'probably close to the interpolation threshold'. That rests on a parameter-count analogy with ResNet18 width 10 on CIFAR, not on any measurement. The 2M and 20M error values are extrapolations from a 4-point fit, which the authors call uncertain.

versions.untested_parts: No model-size sweep or model-wise test-error curve.
No test-error curve over training epochs.
The paper does not measure the sample-size effect near an interpolation threshold; it studies the assumed power-law region.
No capacity sweep or general double-descent curve across model classes.
No test of whether one effective-complexity measure predicts peak locations.
No study of noise, multiple peaks, or optimally tuned regularization.
No comparison of parameter counts with an effective parameter count.

relation.reason: Section 2 discusses previously reported double descent; Section 3.1, footnote 5, explains avoiding the relevant small-data region.

tranche.reason: The experiment measures data scaling in an intended power-law regime, avoiding the small-data region where error can increase; it does not test a double-descent claim version.

source_check.notes: Learning-set sizes include a 90% training/10% validation split; the stated early stop is after 250 epochs. The fitted 16.8% error floor is numerically correct, but the authors explicitly caution that four regression points cannot reliably establish the irreducible error.
